title: Week 5 Tutorials — Live Foley: Multi-Camera Video & Live Sound Workflow
description: These tutorials support the **Live Foley assignment**, focusing on workflows for **multi-camera video editing, audio synchronization, and live sound integration**. Students will use **Premiere Pro** to organize, synchronize, and edit footage from multiple cameras, and **Reaper** to refine, balance, and export the final audiovisual piece. The emphasis is on **clean, well-organized workflows** and **clarity of live sound**, not advanced effects or post-production sound design. Students are expected to rely on prior technical knowledge from earlier weeks and the Audio course, using these tutorials as a focused reference for this project.

title: 🎥 Premiere Pro
description: These tutorials focus on **project organization, multi-camera workflows, and audio-based synchronization** in Adobe Premiere Pro. They will help you efficiently import, organize, sync, and edit footage from multiple cameras for the Live Foley project.

children.title: HOW TO ORGANIZE YOUR PREMIERE PROJECT – Premiere Pro Organization (Filmmaking 101)
children.description: In this video, you will learn how to organize your Adobe Premiere Pro project using bins and clear naming conventions. Proper organization will help you work more efficiently, especially when editing footage from multiple cameras and audio sources.

children.title: How to Edit Multi-Camera Sequences in Premiere Pro (Step-by-Step Tutorial)
children.description: This tutorial walks you through the process of creating and editing a multi-camera sequence in Premiere Pro. You will learn how to synchronize multiple camera angles and switch between them efficiently within a single sequence.

children.title: How to Sync Multiple Clips in Premiere – Fast Editor Pro Tip
children.description: Learn how to synchronize multiple clips in Premiere Pro using audio waveforms. This method is especially useful when working with multiple cameras and a hand clap for sync, as required for the Live Foley project.

children.title: How to Edit Multi-Camera Sequences Easily in Adobe Premiere Pro CC
children.description: This creator-focused tutorial offers an alternative perspective on multi-camera editing, emphasizing practical workflow tips and shortcuts for switching between camera angles during the edit.

children.title: How to do picture in picture premiere pro?
children.description: Picture-in-picture (PiP) in Premiere Pro lets you overlay one video clip on top of another, usually in a smaller window. This effect is commonly used for commentary, reactions, or multitasking visuals, allowing viewers to see two clips at once with one featured prominently and the other in a corner.

title: 🎧 Reaper
description: These tutorials support **basic video import, audio synchronization, level balancing, and export workflows** in Reaper. Students are expected to **rely primarily on the Reaper tutorials and foundational audio knowledge from the previous Audio course**, using these videos as a refresher and reference rather than learning Reaper from scratch.

children.title: Importing Video in Reaper
children.description: Learn how to import a video file into Reaper so you can work directly with image and sound together. This is required for syncing your live Foley recordings and preparing your final export.

children.title: How to Import and Export Video Files in Reaper
children.description: This tutorial covers the full workflow for importing video into Reaper and exporting your final audiovisual file, including checking levels before export.

children.title: Removing Background Noise in Reaper (ReaFIR)
children.description: Optional troubleshooting tutorial demonstrating basic background noise reduction using ReaFIR. Use **sparingly** and only if necessary—your primary focus should be on clean live recording rather than heavy post-processing.

children.title: Normalization in Reaper
children.description: Learn how to normalize individual items, tracks, and mixes in Reaper. This tutorial also explains common normalization pitfalls, such as unintended peaking when normalizing to LUFS levels.
